title: BoKA: Bayesian Optimization based Knowledge Amalgamation for Multi-unknown-domain Text Classification

problem.claim: Performance of domain-specialized finetuned models may degrade on a fresh dataset covering multiple unknown subdomains, while selecting suitable teacher-model combinations is difficult.

gap.claim: Classical knowledge amalgamation relies on tedious and inefficient manual teacher-model selection, and automated combination selection for text classification had not been explored.

contributions.claim: The study introduces an automated combination-selection process for knowledge amalgamation in text classification.

narrative_sequence.summary: Many finetuned language models specialized in distinct domains are available online.
These models may perform worse on fresh datasets spanning multiple subdomains.
Knowledge amalgamation reuses domain-specialized teacher models to train a student model without manual labeling.
Unknown sample domains make teacher selection complicated, and classical approaches use tedious manual selection.
The study proposes automating combination selection for knowledge amalgamation in text classification.

unknowns: The abstract does not report the specific Bayesian optimization procedure.
The abstract does not provide datasets, baselines, quantitative results, or experimental conditions.
